title: Hopscotch kernel harmonizer: per-request kernel hopping with staged autotune
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight runtime component (Hopscotch Kernel Harmonizer) that enables per-request kernel hopping between optimized kernel implementations based on request fingerprinting (arch + sequence-length distribution + prefix characteristics). The goal is to reduce p99 latency regressions and per-token cost for mixed-length workloads by selecting kernels differently for prefill and decode phases and by performing staged autotune experiments with safe rollbacks.
tasks: Define request fingerprint schema (arch, effective seqlen, prefix token distribution, kv-cache size)
Prototype fast probe mode: microbench a small set of candidate kernels on representative prefills during low-traffic windows
Implement hopscotch selector: bandit-style decision with warmstart from historical profiles and explicit safety thresholds
Integrate selection into prefill pipeline and ensure KV cache continuity when hopping between kernels
Add telemetry: per-request kernel chosen, estimated cost delta, latency contribution, rollback counts
Build benchmark harness for mixed seqlen workloads and run canary experiments against baseline kernel selector
Create rollout plan with canary %, kill switches, and automatic fallback to stable kernel
acceptance_criteria: Selector reduces weighted p99 latency by >= 8% on mixed seqlen internal benchmark compared to baseline
No increase in error rate or model output divergence attributable to kernel hopping (acceptance threshold: model churn < 0.2%)
Autotune experiments complete without violating latency SLOs; automatic rollback triggers within 5 minutes on regressions
Metrics emitted per-request and visible in Console runtime dashboard; cost delta reported per route
technical_notes: Hopscotch model: maintain small candidate set per arch/profile. Use Thompson sampling variant with conservative priors to avoid exploratory risk.
Probe strategy: execute micro-probes limited to first N tokens of a low-priority sample, run in isolated microtask that uses warm caches to approximate steady-state throughput.
KV continuity: when switching kernels between prefill and decode, map KV cache layout predictably and validate checksum—if mismatch, trigger safe fallback to original kernel to preserve correctness.
Cost model: incorporate measured per-token GPU time and memory occupancy into reward signal rather than raw latency to favor throughput-efficient kernels under heavy load.
Safety: enforce hard guardrails for tail latency and memory oversubscription. Autotune must not schedule a candidate that increases p99 beyond safe delta.
Data retention: store per-profile rollup summaries for 90 days to warmstart future sessions without keeping raw traces indefinitely.
Interoperability: expose selector hooks so Dedicated and Private deployments can opt into local or central autotuning modes.
notes: This ticket explores a new hybrid approach between static kernel catalogs and full online autotuners. The hopscotch idea attempts cheap, reversible per-request switching rather than wholesale model of global kernel replacement.

We intentionally separate prefill fingerprinting from decode decisions so we can pick a prefill-optimized kernel and, if beneficial, hop to a decode-optimized kernel for remaining tokens while preserving the KV cache semantics.
We must coordinate with runtime scheduling team to ensure probe tasks don't violate isolated tenant quotas.
comments: 2025-02-15 Aisha Patel: Initial proposal posted. Rationale: observed p99 regressions in mixed-chat workloads where long prefill kernels blocked low-latency short requests; hypothesize per-request hopping can reduce tail without global swapping.

2025-02-20 Lena Fischer: Reviewed prototype plan. Suggest limiting candidate set to 3 kernels per arch to bound exploration and avoid oscillation. Will start prototype using existing kernel metadata from ENG-24101.

2025-02-26 Marco Ruiz: Ran microbench: hopscotch probe on sampled talkbot workload shows 10% median token-time improvement and 12% p99 reduction in our internal sim against baseline, probe overhead 0.4% of total tokens.

2025-03-01 QA Notes by Priya Nair: Verified KV continuity tests. Found edge-case where checkpointing and restore between kernels produced mismatch when quantization packing differed; created follow-up subtask to normalize KV packing across candidates.

2025-03-04 Lena Fischer: Implemented basic telemetry and canary job. Rolling out 5% traffic canary for runtime-1.21 with monitor alerts. Blocker: need runtime catalog metadata field for 'kv-packing-format' (dependency created ENG-99098).
